summary: Two things are holding economy at 7.9/8.0. Neither is another colour nudge. (1) The paired q15 camera hides most of what y_47300 shows. I found a camera that frames y_47300 almost exactly (tested, see notForEcon). In that matched view the back colours already match the photo to within a few units (#4b5b89 vs #4b5d8d tick, #2e3a61 vs #2d3c67 fleck). What does not match is texture contrast. (2) The Y fabric tiles lose contrast with distance: they hold up at the q15 hero-row scale (about 480 px/m) but fall to about 0.5-0.7x the photo at 250-300 px/m, the scale of the photo's own near row. Two causes are measured: the tick tile's columns lean 7 deg (cut from the oblique y_47306), so they cancel over a back; and the dark floors (tick 0.15, fleck 0.3) and the 1.25 core exponent flatten the fleck. A tested make_swatches change (variant D) straightens the ticks and lowers the floors. In the matched view it lifts tick p90-p10 from 21 to 30 (photo 33-41) and fleck from 11-15 to 17-21 (photo 26-28). It puts the q15 hero fleck exactly on the photo (29 vs 29), and in the e4 close-up it brings p90-p10 from 43 to 49 (photo 50) without over-sharpening. Ranked econ items: 1 fabric tiles (+0.25); 2 the w20-candidate cover (r 0.3 plastic) reads as grey crinkled foil in q15, so smooth it and drop its normal layer before rating (+0.1, and it avoids a regression); 3 pillow silhouette, too wide and squat (+0.1 once q15 is matched); 4 headrest cover/pad proportion, contingent on question 17 (+0.1). The biggest single lever is the QA camera, which belongs to integration; on its own I would estimate +0.2-0.3. Expected total with the camera: about 8.4-8.7.

items.title: Re-cut the Y fabric tiles so they keep their contrast at row distance: straighten the tick columns (they lean 7 deg), widen the tick pitch to about 13 mm, and stop flattening the fleck and tick darks
items.ladderLevel: value and tone structure at thumbnail scale -> surface texture realism (weave)
items.evidence:
All measurements are L* (0-100) unless noted.

Matched view (camera framed like y_47300, near row about 255 px/m against the photo's 298 px/m; matched_BD.png):
- Tick backs: p90-p10 21-22, p10 28, locStd 7.6, against y_47300 seats 1/3 at 41/33, p10 12-19, locStd 12-15.
- Fleck backs: p90-p10 11-15 against 26-28.
- The mean colours already match: #4b5b89 vs #4b5d8d, #2e3a61 vs #2d3c67, #2b3762 vs #27355b.
- So the gap is contrast, not tone. At thumbnail the photo backs read as crisp vertical columns and pale petals on deep navy; the render reads as soft, lifted mottle.

In q15 at its own 481 px/m the tick already matches (39 vs 41). The loss is distance-dependent, so it comes from the tile's frequency content (plus mip filtering, see notForEcon).

Causes, measured on tex/:
- (a) lean.py: the tick tile's columns lean 7.0 deg, inherited from the oblique y_47306 crop. The column-profile std is 6.8 at 0 deg against 22-33 when de-skewed; the y_47300 columns lean -1 deg, so they are vertical. The 1.6x column lift (c**0.6) has been lifting an almost flat profile.
- (b) The pitch is about 11 mm against about 13 mm in y_47300 (rater A, w18).
- (c) The tile floors lift the darks: tick floor 0.15, fleck 0.3, so the fleck tile's p10/p50 is 0.57/0.78. The fleck core exponent of 1.25 thins the flecks: at 298 px/m the tile shows coverage 0.22 and fleck/ground 2.22 (linear) against 0.30 / 5.0 in y_47300 seats 2/4.
- meso.py, tile CV at 150 px/m: fleck 0.31 vs photo 0.84, tick 0.31 vs 0.46-0.49.

Variant D, tested (build + render, oD/):
- Matched view: tick p90-p10 21 -> 29/31, p10 28 -> 21-23, locStd 7.6 -> 10.8; fleck 15/11 -> 21/17.
- q15 hero fleck seat 2: 18 -> 29 (photo 29); bright fraction 0.09 -> 0.17 (photo 0.14).
- e4 close-up mid back: 43 -> 49 (y_47306 50); dark colour #1b1e47 -> #111442 (photo #0e215c).
- At 300 px/m the tile column CV goes 0.105 -> 0.35 (y_47300 0.26-0.37). At 150 px/m it goes 0.068 -> 0.17 (0.16-0.24).
items.expectedGain: +0.25. This is the fabric item both raters list as medium every round: the tick 'rain streaks' and wandering columns, and the fleck that is 'faint and round at distance'. It moves the hero-row and matched-view contrast onto the photo.
items.fix:
All changes are in test/make_swatches.py, then re-run `python3 test/make_swatches.py y_tick y_fleck y_mosaic`. The tested hooks are in make_swatches_expt.diff.

1. Y_PHOTO['y_tick']: change ('y_47306', (260,385,412,537), 0.249, 14, 0, 0.15, 0.95, 0.15) to (..., 0.29, 14, 7, 0.15, 0.95, 0.05).
   - rot 7 straightens the columns: lean.py on the result gives 0 deg.
   - size 0.29 gives about a 13 mm pitch.
   - floor 0.05 lets the dark channels reach the photo's p10.
   - Set the column-lift exponent in the y_tick branch, c ** 0.6, to 0.0-0.2: with straight columns the profile is real, and 0.6 over-sharpens close up.
2. y_fleck: change the floor from 0.3 to 0.15, and the core exponent (e/ep) ** 1.25 to ** 0.9.
3. Add a meso-band boost in log luminance just before the final normalisation in y_photo:
   lg = log(lum); r *= exp(g*(blur(lg, 5 mm) - blur(lg, 25 mm)) - f*(lg - blur(lg, 1.2 mm)))
   - g/f: tick 1.0/0.3, fleck 1.2/0, mosaic 0.6/0.2.

Acceptance:
- The tile CV at 150 px/m is at least 0.17 column CV (tick) and at least 0.44 CV (fleck).
- In the matched view, tick p90-p10 is at least 29 with p10 at most 22, and fleck p90-p10 is at least 20.
- In e4 the p90-p10 stays at 52 or below.

Update tex/sizes.json (y_tick 0.29). Triangle cost: 0.

items.title: Cover (w20 candidate #262b44 r 0.3 plastic): keep the angle dependence, but make it a smooth sheet, not crinkled grey foil
items.ladderLevel: material response (value structure of the darkest accent)
items.evidence:
I rendered the working tree (6ff75a6 plus the uncommitted yCover change) as oB.

It improves the oblique views:
- q16 row-2 covers: L50 25 -> 36 and p90 29 -> 55, toward y_47301's silver row-2 covers.
- q16 near cover: a bright edge, p95 37 -> 59.

But in q15 the camera looks 24 deg down at covers tilted back 13 deg, so the middle covers mirror the ceiling:
- They measure #6d7082, saturation 0.16, L50 50, with a wavy, hammered reflection pattern (oB/q15_econFronts.png, matched_BD.png middle).
- y_47300 shows #272d48, saturation 0.45, L*19, and a perfectly even surface (p90-p10 4).
- The waviness comes from the LAYER.plastic normal perturbation plus the plate's 4 mm forward bow, both seen through a low-roughness mirror.

An experiment with a metallic satin cover (m 0.75, #58627f) confirmed that the env reflection lifts the cover at every angle in this white cabin, head-on included (q15 L50 55). Low-roughness dielectric is the only econ-side way to get the angle dependence. The flat, mirror-quality surface matters as much as the value.

The e4 studio cover stays near-black at L*18 against 34-52 in y_47306. That is the studio's flat environment, not the material.
items.expectedGain: +0.1. Equally, it avoids a regression of about -0.1 if the foil look ships as is.
items.fix:
SEATMAT.yCover in 09_seats.js (shared file, one line): { c: '#262b44', r: 0.38, l: LAYER.none }.
- LAYER.none removes the normal and roughness noise.
- r 0.38 instead of 0.3 spreads the ceiling reflection into a soft gradient.

In econSeat, cut the plate's forward bow from about 4 mm to at most 1.5 mm. In the plate loft, change z -0.1015/-0.1025/-0.1015 to about -0.1035/-0.104/-0.1035 against -0.111/-0.0985 at the ends; better, make it a straight plate with only the fold rounded.

Acceptance:
- q15 middle covers: saturation at least 0.35, B/R at least 1.6, L50 at most 30 (my L* scale; the raters' L about 45), p90-p10 at most 8.
- q16 row-2 covers: L50 at least 33.

items.title: Pillow silhouette: narrower, taller and more upright, so it reads as four separate puffy dark cushions rather than a dark band across the crease
items.ladderLevel: silhouette and proportion (and the dark accents of the lower third)
items.evidence:
In y_47300 the pillows are the four darkest shapes, in the lower third of the near row (#1c213a-#2c3457, L*12-23).
- Each pillow is about 0.77 of the back width: seat 2 is 98 px on a 128 px back.
- Height/width is about 0.78, with a concave top and pinched corners.
- Each stands against the back with its whole outline visible above the pan.

In the matched render view (q15L_vs_photo.png, oC/q15L zoom) the pillow spans about 0.93 of the back (code: 0.195*2 = 0.39 m of 0.43). Its visible height/width is about 0.44, because the centre sits only about 0.12 m above the pan top while the half-height is 0.145, so about 2.5 cm is buried in the crease and the -76 deg tilt foreshortens the rest. It reads as one dark strip, pan-width, instead of four pillows with pan fabric showing around them.

The raters see this only in e1 / e4b today, because the q15 camera crops it out. It becomes a first-order shape once the camera is fixed (notForEcon 1).
items.fix:
econSeat pillow block in 09a_econ.js:
- Half-width 0.195 -> 0.165 (0.33 m = 0.77 of the back).
- Half-height 0.145 -> 0.135.
- Mount M4.trs(0, 0.15, -0.12, 0, -76*DEG) -> M4.trs(0, 0.19, -0.115, 0, -80*DEG). That raises it about 4 cm, so the bottom just touches the pan, and stands it about 4 deg more upright. Check e4b and q15L that the bottom edge does not float.

Triangle cost: 0 (optional ring about +0.3k per seat).

items.title: Headrest read in the paired photo: the cover sits inside a visibly lighter pad. Contingent on question 17 (y_47300 CG vs the in-service long flap).
items.evidence:
In y_47300 each seat ends in a distinct light pad band:
- The pad ears are L*44-48 against backs of 23-41.
- The pad shows about 2.7 cm above the cover and 5-6 cm at each side.
- The cover is 0.24 x 0.168 m (h/w 0.70) and ends at the pad bottom.
- A shadow line runs under the pad.

In the render the cover is 0.255 x about 0.235 (h/w 0.92) and hangs about 3 cm below the pad. In the matched view the pad is only thin slivers either side (matched_BD.png), so the light top band of every seat, the most regular light-dark rhythm in y_47300's far rows, is missing.

The in-service photos disagree (cover h/w 0.86-0.88 and a long hang: y_47301, y_47302, y_47306), which is why this waits on the user.

notForEcon.issue:
Integration owns this, and it is the largest lever: q15 does not frame y_47300. y_47300 is shot from the door-4 cross aisle, about 2.6 m behind the first full centre row (row 31, z 47.0). The 64 deg hfov puts the 4-seat block at about 60 % of the frame, and the horizon is about 12 deg above centre. Our cabin has the door-4 centre galley at that spot, so a near-plane clip is needed.

Tested in a scratch copy:
`(()=>{const P=M4.perspective; M4.perspective=(f,a,n,fa)=>P(f,a,Math.max(n,1.45),fa); __app.setView([0,1.62,44.45],Math.PI,-0.20);})()`
This gives q15L_vs_photo.png, which shows the near row with pillows, pans and arms and the far rows to the bulkhead, as in the photo.

- Restore M4.perspective afterwards (it leaked into the next view), or add an app-level near-plane override.
- Fine-tune: z about 44.85 with clip about 1.1 (the backs are about 110 px vs 128-150 in the photo), and pitch about -0.16.
- Expect it to expose the under-seat white parts and the floor-path light lines, which are dark in the photo.

q16 (across the cabin vs y_47301 down the aisle) and q17 (high rear view vs y_47303's window-side profile) are still mismatched, as both raters note every round.

Texture minification: the photo fabric layers (16, 24, 25, 26) lose 30-50 % of their contrast between 480 and 250 px/m. A texture LOD bias of about -0.75 on the u_photo lookups (texture(u_photo, vec3(...), -0.75)), or textureGrad with the derivatives scaled by 0.6, would keep the tick columns and the flecks. It adds to rank 1.

Leatherette sheen: a Charlie or velvet sheen lobe on the cover material would give the silver-grey grazing look of y_47301 / 47303 / 47306 (e4 cover L*18 vs 34-52) without the mirror. Econ can only use low-roughness Fresnel (rank 2).

In the matched view the darkest fabric tones are lifted: tick-back p10 is L*28 (21 with variant D) against 12-19 in y_47300, and the dark colour is #2e396d against #0d1f4e. Most of this is now fixable in the tile (rank 1); the rest is ambient fill / AO between the rows.
